title: A Tide for the Orchard
premise: Edmund Eriksen, a ghostwriter who built his career erasing himself from other people's stories, is hired to pen the memoirs of rival author Vivian Marsh — while falling for her estranged sister, orchard-bakery owner June Calloway, whom he first recruited as a fake date to survive the Eriksen family reunion. As Edmund's ghostwritten chapters begin cannibalizing details from June's life and her bakery's lease deadline looms, he must decide whether to expose Vivian's plagiarism of June's unpublished family recipes-and-memoir manuscript or protect the career that once saved him. At the climax, Edmund publicly credits June at Vivian's book launch, sacrificing his anonymity and his contract; in the end, June's lease is saved by the memoir's royalties redirected to her, and the two open a writing nook above the bakery together.
about_author: I. M. Pemberton is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper columnist who spent a decade writing other people's obituaries, wedding announcements, and one anonymously published romance. Pemberton now lives beside an actual orchard, insisting that all the best love stories ripen late.

chapters.title: The Ghost at the Reunion Table
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Desperate to dodge his family's pitying questions about his stalled novel, Edmund hires June Calloway — a stranger selling cider donuts outside the venue — to pose as his girlfriend for one afternoon. The fake date works too well: by dessert they're finishing each other's sentences, and Edmund's mother has already invited June to Christmas. Emotional beat: reluctant delight, the first crack in Edmund's armor.

chapters.title: Manuscript and Marzipan
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Edmund begins ghostwriting Vivian Marsh's memoir while secretly dating June, whose failing orchard bakery faces a lease deadline. When June shares her family's stories and recipes over late nights in the kitchen, Edmund recognizes them verbatim in Vivian's draft — Vivian bought June's rejected manuscript years ago. Emotional beat: warmth curdling into dread as love and livelihood collide.

chapters.title: What the Orchard Remembers
chapters.summary: June's POV. June discovers Edmund's connection to Vivian and believes he's been harvesting her life for material all along. She ends things days before the lease decision, and Edmund, bound by a crushing NDA, can't explain without destroying his career. He drafts a confession letter he may never send. Emotional beat: heartbreak and betrayal, with duty tightening like a vise around both of them.

chapters.title: A Tide for the Orchard
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV, closing on shared narration. At Vivian's glittering launch, Edmund takes the microphone, breaks his NDA, and names June as the true author before the press. The fallout costs him his contract but forces Vivian's publisher to settle — royalties that save the bakery's lease. June finds him afterward among the apple trees, and this time nothing is pretend. Emotional beat: sacrifice rewarded, justice outside the law, love chosen at last.
